content.key_idea: Although a dataflow circuit's full state space is formally defined using unbounded input sequences, a small bounded sequence length (here N=2) already reaches every one of the circuit's 7 states, so finite test sequences suffice for exhaustive equivalence checking.

evidence: Figure 5b reports all 7 states of the circuit (in the blue box)
When each Source produces sequences with N = 1, the states framed with a red box (states 5–7) are all the reachable states
When each Source produces sequences with N = 2, the computed state space is the same as the one using infinite token sequence length

summary: This figure justifies why ElasticMiter can use bounded, finite input sequences instead of unbounded ones when computing a dataflow circuit's full state space. Panel (a) shows the test circuit: two Sources (each emitting a token sequence, optionally bounded to N tokens) feed non-deterministic delays (ND0, ND1), one of which passes through a Buffer (Buf1, the component under test from Figure 4's LHS) before reaching a shared Branch component, then more delays (ND2, ND3) to two Sinks. Panel (b) enumerates all 7 states this circuit can reach, one small numbered box per state, each showing the same Branch template with different token contents (0 or 1) occupying its slots. A blue outer boundary marks that all 7 states are reached once each Source's sequence length N reaches 2 (equivalent to unbounded, N=infinity); a nested red boundary shows that bounding N to 1 reaches only states 5-7, missing states 1-4. This nesting demonstrates that a sufficiently large but still finite N (here 2) already covers the entire reachable state space, so ElasticMiter's Buffers can be sized to a finite, determined length rather than needing unbounded sequences.
summary_zh: 该图说明为何ElasticMiter可用有限长度的输入序列代替无限序列：(a)电路含两个Source经不确定延迟ND0/ND1、缓冲器Buf1，汇入Branch后经ND2/ND3到两个Sink；(b)枚举该电路全部7个可达状态，每个状态框显示Branch上0/1令牌的不同占位；蓝色外框表示N=2（等价于N=∞）已覆盖全部7个状态，内层红框表示N=1仅能到达状态5-7，说明有限长度足以覆盖完整状态空间。
